findings.title: Validate a locked destination before debiting the source
findings.explanation: A transfer to an existing account whose `id` starts with `locked-` now debits `from.balanceCents` before throwing `destination locked`. The exception prevents the credit, so a rejected transfer permanently leaves the two balances inconsistent. This directly regresses the required all-or-nothing transfer behavior; move the destination validation before either balance mutation (or otherwise make the mutation atomic).
findings.failurePath: With a funded source, an existing locked destination, and a positive `cents` value: `from.balanceCents -= cents` executes, the following locked-destination check throws, and execution never reaches `to.balanceCents += cents`.

candidates.invariant: A transfer must either complete the debit and credit together or leave both balances unchanged.
candidates.counterexample: With a funded source and a destination whose ID starts with locked-, the function subtracts cents from the source, then throws destination locked before crediting the destination.
candidates.evidenceNeeded: Confirm callers and tests assume rejected transfers are non-mutating and provide no compensating rollback.

candidates.invariant: Validation failures must occur before state mutation so exception paths are safe to retry or recover.
candidates.counterexample: A locked destination causes an exception after the source balance has already been reduced, leaving the ledger in a partially applied state.
candidates.evidenceNeeded: Check whether any caller catches destination locked and compensates for the prior debit.

The exception prevents the credit, so a rejected transfer permanently leaves the two balances inconsistent. This directly regresses the required all-or-nothing transfer behavior; move the destination validation before either balance mutation (or otherwise make the mutation atomic).
